additional_requirements: depressive_episode is present for the majority of the total duration of the active and residual portions of the illness (Criterion C)
delusions_and_hallucinations occur for 2 or more weeks in the absence of a major mood episode (Criterion B)

S019.name: Delusions
S019.description: Fixed beliefs that do not change easily, even in the face of contradictory evidence.

subtypes.Persecutory Delusions: The false belief that one is being harmed or monitored by other people or organizations.
subtypes.Referential Delusions: The conviction that ordinary events, remarks, or behaviors have specific relevance to oneself.
subtypes.Grandiose Delusions: The false belief that one possesses special abilities, power, or fame.
subtypes.Erotomanic Delusions: The false belief that another person is in love with or has affection for them.
subtypes.Nihilistic Delusions: A destructive or negative conviction that the world is ending or that a major catastrophe will occur.
subtypes.Somatic Delusions: The baseless conviction that there is a serious abnormality with one's body or organs.
subtypes.Jealous Delusions: The conviction that one's spouse or romantic partner is being unfaithful without sufficient evidence.

S020.name: Hallucinations
S020.description: Perception-like experiences that occur without an external stimulus and are as vivid and clear as normal perception.

subtypes.Auditory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of hearing voices or sounds when there is no actual sound.
subtypes.Visual Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of seeing people or objects that do not exist.
subtypes.Tactile Hallucinations: Experiencing the sensation of being touched or movement on the skin when there is no actual stimulus.
subtypes.Olfactory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of smelling odors that do not exist.
subtypes.Gustatory Hallucinations: The perceptual experience of tasting flavors that are not actually present.

S023.name: Negative_Symptoms
S023.description: A state where emotions, motivation, speech, or social interest that should normally be present are diminished or lost.

subtypes.Diminished Emotional Expression: A state of reduced emotional expression in facial expressions, eye contact, intonation of speech, and movements.
subtypes.Avolition: A decrease in motivated self-initiated purposeful activities.
subtypes.Alogia: A state where the quantity of spontaneous speech is significantly reduced.
subtypes.Anhedonia: A decrease in the ability to experience pleasure or interest in enjoyable activities.
subtypes.Asociality: A state where interest in social activities or interpersonal relationships is significantly reduced.

S024.name: Depressed_Mood
S024.description: A state where a sad, empty, or hopeless mood persists.

subtypes.Depressed Mood: A persistently sunken mood or feeling of depression.
subtypes.Tearfulness: A state of frequent crying or inability to hold back tears.
subtypes.Sadness: A state where a sad or gloomy mood is maintained continuously.
subtypes.Emptiness: A feeling of inner emptiness or a state of feeling no emotion.
subtypes.Emotional Numbness: A state where emotions feel dulled or paralyzed.

S026.name: Weight_Appetite_Change
S026.description: Significant increase or decrease in appetite or weight.

subtypes.Significant Weight Loss: Weight loss of more than 5% in a month without dieting.
subtypes.Weight Gain: Weight gain of more than 5% in a month.
subtypes.Decrease in Appetite: Decrease in appetite occurring nearly every day.
subtypes.Increase in Appetite: Increase in appetite occurring nearly every day.

S028.name: Psychomotor_Changes
S028.description: Observable increase or decrease in psychomotor activity.

subtypes.Psychomotor Agitation: Purposeless repetitive behaviors such as inability to sit still, pacing, hand-wringing, or picking at skin.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Motor): Visible slowing of general body movements, such as walking speed or picking up objects.
subtypes.Psychomotor Retardation (Speech): Long response latency or slowed speech when asked a question.

S030.name: Worthlessness_Guilt
S030.description: Feelings of worthlessness or excessive or inappropriate guilt (which may be delusional; not merely self-reproach or guilt about being sick).

subtypes.Feelings of Worthlessness: The feeling that one is useless and has no value.
subtypes.Ruminative Guilt: A thought pattern of obsessively replaying past minor mistakes or flaws and constantly reproaching oneself.
subtypes.Excessive or Inappropriate Guilt: Feeling excessive responsibility for trivial matters or daily events and believing one deserves punishment.
subtypes.Delusional Guilt: Guilt reaching a delusional level, disconnected from reality, involving feeling responsible for unrelated unfortunate events.

S031.name: Diminished_Thinking
S031.description: Diminished ability to think or concentrate, or indecisiveness.

subtypes.Reduced Concentration: Unable to pay attention or maintain focus on specific activities like conversation, reading, or watching TV.
subtypes.Indecisiveness: Extreme difficulty making even minor daily choices (e.g., menu, clothes) and hesitating to make decisions.
subtypes.Subjective Memory Complaints: Complaining of memory decline, such as forgetting where things were placed, due to reduced focus.
subtypes.Clouded Thinking: Thinking feels foggy, dazed, or not clear.

S032.name: Death_Suicide
S032.description: Recurrent thoughts of death, recurrent suicidal ideation, or a suicide attempt.

subtypes.Recurrent Thoughts of Death: Passive wish to die (e.g., 'I wish I wouldn't wake up') without active intent to kill oneself.
subtypes.Suicidal Ideation: Recurring thoughts of 'I want to die' or 'I want to kill myself' without a specific plan.
subtypes.Suicidal Impulse: Strong, sudden urges to jump from a height or run into traffic without a concrete plan.
subtypes.Specific Plan for Suicide: Conceiving specific scenarios or methods regarding when, where, and how to die.
subtypes.Suicide Attempt: Actual actions taken to end one's life or preparatory behaviors like hoarding pills or writing a will.

info.persona: Deborah Lewing is a routine‑driven, compassionate young stylist whose meticulous nature and love for solitary reflection shape every facet of their life, from precise haircuts to thoughtful budgeting.
info.professional_persona: Deborah Lewing, a 21‑year‑old with an associate’s degree in cosmetology aspiring to own a boutique salon in Berkeley, blends precision haircutting, balanced color formulation, and meticulous sanitation with a methodical, routine‑driven mindset that ensures each client receives a consistently high‑quality experience, and they mentor junior staff with compassionate communication.
info.cultural_background: Deborah was raised in a middle‑class, white family in the Bay Area, where her parents emphasized diligence, practicality, and community service. Her upbringing blended traditional American values—such as celebrating Thanksgiving and the Fourth of July with family gatherings—with the progressive, environmentally conscious culture of Berkeley. She regularly shops at local farmer’s markets, participates in neighborhood clean‑up events, and values inclusive community initiatives. This cultural mix nurtured her respect for routine and order while fostering a compassionate, cooperative mindset that guides her personal and professional life.
info.hobbies_and_interests: In her free time, Deborah enjoys solitary yet grounding activities that complement her preference for routine. She journals each evening, noting reflections on client interactions and personal goals. Reading classic literature and poetry provides a calm escape, while weekend hikes in the Berkeley hills connect her with nature. She tends to a small indoor garden of herbs and succulents, practices gentle yoga to maintain resilience, and occasionally knits scarves for friends and charitable drives. Deborah volunteers at a local senior center, offering free haircuts and listening ear, and she frequents neighborhood coffee shops to sample seasonal brews and observe the community.
info.sports_persona: Deborah Lewing enjoys weekend hikes with the Berkeley Hiking Club, practices gentle yoga three times a week at a local studio, follows the Golden State Warriors during the NBA season, and prefers low‑intensity, routine‑based fitness activities that fit their organized schedule.
info.arts_persona: Deborah Lewing often escapes into classic literature, savoring poems by Emily Dickinson and novels by Jane Austen, while their coffee‑shop playlists feature folk singer Sufjan Stevens and indie pianist Nils Frahm, and they occasionally attend productions of Shakespeare at the Berkeley Repertory Theatre, which inform their aesthetic sensibility in client styling.
info.travel_persona: Deborah Lewing prefers carefully planned, low‑cost escapes, returning each summer to the red‑wood trails of Mendocino and weekend road‑tripping to Napa Valley for wine tasting, while dreaming of a future solo trip to Kyoto to study traditional art and a spring backpacking adventure through the Swiss Alps, all budgeted through a dedicated travel fund.
info.culinary_persona: Deborah Lewing enjoys crafting simple herb‑infused meals, regularly preparing rosemary‑garlic roasted potatoes, basil pesto pasta, and avocado toast topped with microgreens, while they frequent neighborhood cafés for seasonal pour‑over brews like hazelnut latte, using fresh mint and thyme from their indoor garden to flavor home‑cooked dishes.

info.persona: Ricardo Vazquez, a quietly competitive data‑driven restaurateur, balances solitary culinary experiments with methodical career ambition, while they occasionally neglect social obligations in favor of vintage coffee grinder hunts and meticulous health tracking.
info.professional_persona: An analytical restaurant operations specialist, Ricardo Vazquez leverages bilingual fluency, POS mastery, and meticulous inventory tracking to streamline service workflows, while their introverted, methodical nature drives them to design quiet, efficient dining environments as they prepare for a supervisory role.
info.cultural_background: Ricardo is a first‑generation Mexican‑American who grew up in a bilingual household in Southern California. His family’s traditions—such as celebrating Día de los Muertos, preparing home‑cooked mole, and valuing close‑knit family bonds—have shaped his appreciation for authentic Mexican flavors and community rituals. While he respects these cultural roots, his introverted disposition leads him to engage with his heritage through personal cooking, music, and occasional participation in local cultural festivals, rather than large social gatherings. His Mexican background also informs his work ethic, emphasizing reliability, hospitality, and pride in delivering quality service.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Ricardo enjoys solitary activities that satisfy his curiosity and need for quiet. He spends evenings reading non‑fiction books on behavioral economics and culinary history, and he follows online courses in data analytics and sustainable food systems. On weekends he hikes the nearby San Bernardino foothills, practices acoustic guitar, and experiments with traditional Mexican recipes at home. He also collects vintage coffee grinders and curates a personal library of documentaries about global food cultures.
info.sports_persona: An avid outdoor enthusiast, Ricardo Vazquez spends weekends hiking the San Bernardino foothills with the local San Bernardino Hiking Club, follows the Los Angeles Dodgers, Los Angeles Lakers, and LA Galaxy with quiet devotion, and they maintain a solo fitness routine that includes trail runs and occasional tennis matches at the community courts.
info.arts_persona: A reflective music and documentary aficionado, Ricardo Vazquez dedicates evenings to playing acoustic guitar renditions of José González and Nina Simone, curates a growing collection of vintage coffee grinders while appreciating the cinematic scores of Gustavo Santaolalla, and they regularly watch food‑culture documentaries by Anthony Bourdain and Moby, allowing them to weave cultural storytelling into their creative life.
info.travel_persona: A methodical traveler, Ricardo Vazquez prefers low‑key, self‑crafted itineraries that balance adventure with tranquility, having explored Oaxaca’s mole markets, trekked the cliffs of Patagonia, and soaked in the quiet tea houses of Kyoto, while they plan future trips to the vineyards of Mendoza and the historic streets of Seville, always budgeting carefully to avoid overspending.
info.culinary_persona: A meticulous home chef, Ricardo Vazquez experiments with traditional mole, chipotle‑infused adobo, and smoked corn tortillas, sources heirloom chilies and fresh cacao for authentic flavors, brews single‑origin espresso using a vintage French press, and they treat each cooking session as a data‑driven experiment, meticulously noting ingredient ratios and cooking times in a personal notebook.

info.persona: Jessie Joseph is a community‑driven traffic safety pro whose love of garden harvests, gospel melodies, and spontaneous block parties fuels a resilient yet delightfully disorganized spirit, and they constantly balance structure with spontaneity.
info.professional_persona: Jessie Joseph, a seasoned traffic safety specialist in Kern County’s transportation division, blends meticulous knowledge of road‑closure protocols and first‑aid certification with a natural flair for community outreach, using their talkative, resilient nature to train flaggers, resolve on‑site conflicts, and keep safety procedures organized—though they sometimes let a relaxed attitude toward strict deadlines lead to last‑minute paperwork sprints.
info.cultural_background: Jessie's cultural background is deeply rooted in African‑American traditions of California's Central Valley. Raised in a close‑knit Black community in Bakersfield, she grew up attending church, listening to gospel and soul music, and celebrating family gatherings with rich culinary customs. Her family traces its heritage to the Great Migration, and she maintains strong ties to local Black cultural organizations and churches in Kern County. These experiences have shaped her resilient outlook, communal values, and love for storytelling. Living in Lancaster, she embraces the multicultural environment while acting as a cultural bridge between diverse groups, drawing on her heritage to foster connection and understanding.
info.hobbies_and_interests: Jessie enjoys a vibrant social life that reflects her talkative and community‑oriented personality. She sings in a local gospel choir, organizes neighborhood block parties, and volunteers at the community center teaching arts workshops. Gardening is a favorite pastime; she cultivates heirloom tomatoes and herbs, often sharing the harvest with neighbors. In quiet moments she reads contemporary African‑American fiction, explores nearby desert trails on hikes, and cooks soul‑food meals for family gatherings. She loves dancing to funk and R&B, playing bridge at the senior center, and attending cultural festivals that celebrate Black heritage.
info.sports_persona: Jessie Joseph, an avid desert‑trail hiker and weekend dancer, maintains an active membership in the Kern County Hiking Association, follows the Los Angeles Lakers and Los Angeles Dodgers, and regularly volunteers to coach a youth basketball league, though they occasionally miss gym sessions after late‑night garden parties.
info.arts_persona: Jessie Joseph, a soulful gospel choir member with a passion for funk, sings with the Harmony Gospel Choir, collects vinyl records by James Brown and Erykah Badu, enjoys performances by the National Cultural Theatre, reads contemporary novels by Toni Morrison and Colson Whitehead, and they let these artistic influences shape their community art workshops.
info.travel_persona: Jessie Joseph, who prefers spontaneous road trips over rigid itineraries, has explored Death Valley's desert dunes, the coastal charm of Santa Barbara, and the jazz‑rich streets of New Orleans, and they envision their future adventures trekking the Atlas Mountains in Morocco and attending the vibrant Carnival in Rio de Janeiro.
info.culinary_persona: Jessie Joseph, an enthusiastic home cook, whips up soul‑food classics like fried catfish with hushpuppies, collard greens seasoned with smoked turkey, and sweet‑potato pie, while also cultivating heirloom tomatoes, basil, and thyme in their garden to create fresh garden‑to‑table salads, though they sometimes over‑salt dishes in the excitement of feeding neighbors.
